blurb: Massive British guardian with a black mask, counted the heaviest dog breed
description: The English Mastiff is a very large British dog breed with a massive head, short fawn, apricot or brindle coat, black mask and a gentle, docile nature.
answer: The English Mastiff, often simply called the Mastiff, is a British breed of very large mastiff-type dog and the largest dog breed by mass. It typically stands about 70 to 76 cm tall and can weigh from roughly 54 to over 100 kg. Breed standards describe it as courageous yet docile, gentle and loyal.

body: The Mastiff likely descends from the ancient Alaunt and the Pugnax Britanniae of Roman-era Britain, with significant input from the Alpine Mastiff in the 19th century. Mastiff-type dogs were long used for guarding and hunting, and also in the blood sports that Britain banned in 1835. Systematic breeding by J. W. Thompson and T. V. H. Lukey from the 1830s produced the modern breed, and the AKC recognized it in 1885. The breed nearly disappeared after the Second World War and was rebuilt from a very small number of dogs; it is still classed as vulnerable in the UK, with only 104 registered births in 2020.

The Mastiff has a massive body, a broad, square-looking head, and a body longer than it is tall. The short, close-lying coat is fawn or apricot, or those colors with black brindling, always with a black mask on the muzzle, ears and nose. Long-haired Mastiffs, called Fluffies, occasionally occur through a recessive gene. The heaviest dog ever recorded, at 155.6 kg, was an English Mastiff named Zorba.
Formal standards and historical writers describe a dog combining grandeur and good nature, courage and docility. The American Kennel Club calls Mastiffs powerful yet gentle and loyal dogs.

Because of their size and need for space, the AKC considers Mastiffs best suited to country or suburban life. Sources give little detail on exercise or grooming. Owners are generally advised to keep such a heavy dog at a healthy weight, since obesity is among the problems reported in the breed.

Conditions reported in the breed include hip dysplasia, gastric torsion, obesity, osteosarcoma and cystinuria, with cardiomyopathy, entropion and progressive retinal atrophy seen occasionally. A UK study found a life expectancy of 9 years.

faq.q: How big does an English Mastiff get?
faq.a: Mastiffs typically stand about 70 to 76 cm at the shoulder and weigh from around 54 to over 100 kg, making them the heaviest breed on average.

faq.q: How long do English Mastiffs live?
faq.a: A UK study found a life expectancy of 9 years for the breed.

faq.q: Are English Mastiffs good family dogs?
faq.a: Breed descriptions call them gentle, loyal and docile, but their great size means they need plenty of space.

faq.q: Is the English Mastiff recognized by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as the Mastiff, breed number 264 in Group 2.
